title: Sign the partner agreement and split the promote
summary: Agree among the principals on ownership, decisions, time commitments, the promote split and what happens if someone leaves.

steps.title: Write the term sheet with the default rule beside each term
steps.instruction: Draft the principals' term sheet with one line for each field of the sponsor operating agreement, and beside each write the rule that applies if the agreement is silent. In Texas, profits, losses and distributions follow the agreed value of contributions; each member has an equal vote; no member may withdraw or be expelled; admitting a member and amending the agreement need every member's consent; and an assignee gets economic rights but no say in management. In Delaware, allocations, distributions, assignment, admission and amendment work alike, but members vote by their share of profits, more than half controlling, each member can bind the company, and no member may resign before dissolution. Texas lets the agreement change most defaults, but not the writing rule for promises to contribute, the limit on distributions or the records duty, among others. If an agreement is already signed, write each change as an amendment.
steps.modeBasis: Drafting a term sheet and reading the defaults from the statutes is drafting an agent can do; the principals decide every term.

steps.title: Settle each principal's ownership, capital and later contributions
steps.instruction: The principals settle what each owns, what each puts in and when, and what happens if one does not fund. Record each contribution, whether cash, property or services, with an agreed value, because unless the agreement says otherwise that value sets the split of profits and distributions. Say whether later contributions are required, on which events or dates, or only voluntary. In Texas a promise to contribute is enforceable only if it is in writing and signed by the person promising, and the agreement may provide that a member who does not fund has its interest reduced, subordinated, sold, redeemed at an appraised or formula value or forfeited, or that the others lend the shortfall; Delaware allows the same kinds of consequences. Record each choice on the term sheet.
steps.modeBasis: What each principal owns and pays in is the principals' decision; an agent records it on the term sheet.

steps.title: Settle roles, outside work, signing authority and the decisions that need a vote
steps.instruction: The principals settle who manages, who decides and what each may do outside the firm. Choose management by the members or by named managers; Texas reads the agreement first, then the certificate of formation. Write each principal's role, time commitment, outside real estate work allowed, whether a deal one finds must be offered to the firm first, and what each may sign alone: contracts, loan documents, wires, offering documents. List the major decisions that need a vote, such as admitting a member, taking on a new deal, borrowing, guaranties, selling the company and amending the agreement, with the vote each needs. Absent other terms, Texas acts by majority at a meeting with a quorum, needs a majority of all governing persons outside the ordinary course and of all members for a fundamental business transaction, and accepts written consents.
steps.modeBasis: Who manages and what needs a vote are the principals' decisions; an agent records them on the term sheet.

steps.title: Split the promote and fees among the principals and set vesting
steps.instruction: The principals decide how the promote from each deal, and each fee the firm earns, is divided among them, and whether shares are fixed firm-wide or set deal by deal. To see what is being divided, run a deal's terms through the waterfall-promote calculator at its several endings; the promote it shows is the pool to split. Decide whether each share vests over time, by deal or at a sale, what happens to an unvested share when a principal leaves, and whether a share earned in a deal that has already closed is kept. Texas lets the agreement create classes of interests with their own rights, which can keep a promote interest apart from a capital interest. Record each choice for the tax adviser.
steps.modeBasis: Dividing the economics is the principals' decision; the calculator shows the size of the pool.

steps.title: For a fund, split the fee and the carry entity by entity
steps.instruction: For a fund, the economics sit in separate entities, so settle each split on its own. The management company earns the management fee and pays the team, so its company agreement divides fee income and costs. Each fund's general partner or managing member entity holds that fund's carried interest, so its own agreement divides the carry, sets its vesting and says what a principal keeps in earlier funds after leaving; the waterfall-promote calculator, run in whole-fund order, shows the carry being divided. Decide whether every principal holds an interest in each general partner entity or only those who work on that fund, and who funds the general partner's own commitment. Keep each split consistent with the fund agreement's carry terms. Counsel drafts each of these agreements with the sponsor operating agreement, and every principal who holds an interest in an entity signs its agreement.
steps.modeBasis: How each entity's economics are divided is the principals' decision; an agent records it.

steps.title: For a joint venture, split the venture's promote and fees among the principals
steps.instruction: In a joint venture, settle how the firm's member entity divides the venture's promote and fees among the principals. The promote the venture agreement pays goes to that member entity, and its company agreement divides it. Settle each principal's share of that promote and of any fees the venture pays the firm, who funds the member entity's share of the venture's capital, and who signs any guaranty the lender requires, with any sharing or indemnity among the principals for it. Keep the split consistent with the terms in negotiate-jv-agreement, and settle it before that agreement is signed. Counsel drafts that entity's company agreement with these terms, and every principal who holds an interest in it signs it.
steps.modeBasis: How the member entity's share is divided is the principals' decision; an agent records it.

steps.title: Have the tax adviser settle how each principal's interest is taxed
steps.instruction: Send the term sheet to the tax adviser, who answers in writing how each principal's interest is taxed and its transfer date. Property received for services is taxed at vesting unless an 83(b) election within 30 days of transfer taxes it at receipt. Subject to the exceptions in Rev. Proc. 93-27, the IRS does not tax receiving a profits interest for services to a partnership as a partner; an unvested one is tested at grant, with no election, if the holder is treated as owner from grant and reports its share of income, no one deducts its value, and 93-27's other conditions are met. Section 1061 makes long-term gain on a promote interest short-term unless long-term under a three-year holding period, election or not; its regulations exclude section 1231 gain from the holder's share. The adviser recommends a partnership representative, whose acts bind the company and partners in IRS audits.
steps.modeBasis: How each interest is taxed is a judgment for a licensed tax adviser; an agent sends the term sheet and records the answer.

steps.title: Settle what happens when a principal leaves, dies, divorces or is disabled
steps.instruction: The principals settle each way a principal can leave: resignation, removal for stated cause, disability, death and divorce. For each, say whether the company or the others may or must buy the interest, how the price is set and paid, and what the departing principal keeps in deals already made. Absent such terms, a Texas member cannot withdraw or be expelled, and a Delaware member cannot resign before dissolution. On a Texas member's death or divorce, the spouse or heirs become assignees of their share, and the statute does not impair an agreement to buy or sell an interest on death or divorce. A membership interest may be community property, and property held during marriage is presumed to be, so ask counsel whether each married principal's spouse should sign a consent. The key-principal-leaves situation relies on these terms.
steps.modeBasis: Departure and buyout terms are the principals' decision; an agent records them and counsel answers the spousal question.

steps.title: Settle how a deadlock among the principals is broken
steps.instruction: The principals settle how a tie on a decision the business needs is broken, step by step: a set time to meet and decide, a named tie-breaker or outside adviser for named kinds of decisions, then mediation, then a way out, such as one principal naming a price at which the other must buy or sell, or a sale of the company. Say who runs each existing deal while a dispute lasts. If the principals stay stuck, a Texas court may, on an owner's application, order an LLC wound up when it is not reasonably practicable to carry on its business in conformity with its governing documents, and a Delaware court may dissolve an LLC on the same ground. The sponsor-partners-disagree situation relies on these terms.
steps.modeBasis: How ties are broken is the principals' decision; an agent records it on the term sheet.

steps.title: Have counsel draft the agreement, its duty terms and any covenant
steps.instruction: Send counsel the approved term sheet, the tax adviser's answers, the certificate of formation and any agreement already signed; counsel drafts the agreement or an amendment and restatement, with any spousal consents, and marks each departure from the term sheet. Texas lets the agreement expand, restrict or eliminate duties, including fiduciary duties, and Delaware allows the same except that the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing cannot be eliminated, so counsel writes the outside-work and deal-opportunity terms with that in mind. A Texas covenant not to compete is enforceable only if it is ancillary to or part of an otherwise enforceable agreement and reasonable in time, area and scope of activity, restraining no more than needed to protect goodwill or another business interest; a court reforms one that goes further. Counsel says which state's law governs each covenant.
steps.modeBasis: Drafting enforceable duty, covenant and buyout terms is licensed legal work; an agent assembles the package.

steps.title: Check the draft against the term sheet clause by clause
steps.instruction: Compare the draft with the term sheet line by line: ownership and classes, contributions and the remedies for not funding, management and signing authority, each major decision and its vote, the promote and fee split, vesting, departure and buyout, deadlock, duties and covenants, transfers, amendment, tax matters and the partnership representative. Check that the draft's shares of the promote and fees add to the whole and match the term sheet. List each difference with its clause, and each term-sheet line the draft leaves out, for the principals and counsel to resolve. Check that the company's name matches the filed certificate exactly.
steps.modeBasis: Comparing a draft with a term sheet is document work; the principals and counsel resolve each difference.

steps.title: Prepare each 83(b) election the tax adviser advised
steps.instruction: For each principal the tax adviser advised to elect, prepare the section 83(b) election from the adviser's written answer: the principal's name and address, a description of the interest, the date of transfer and the taxable year, the restrictions on it, its fair market value at transfer without regard to restrictions that will lapse, and the amount paid. Use IRS Form 15620, or a statement signed by the principal that says it is made under section 83(b), gives the same items and says copies have been given to the company. Leave the taxpayer identification number for the principal to enter. Have it ready to sign on the transfer date, calendar the 30th day after the transfer as the last day to mail, and calendar each vesting date in the agreement. The adviser checks the values before the principal signs.
steps.modeBasis: Filling the form from the adviser's written values and building the calendar is drafting; the principal enters the tax number and signs.

steps.title: Every principal signs the agreement, with any spousal consents
steps.instruction: Once every difference is resolved, each principal signs and dates the agreement, and any spousal consent counsel called for is signed. Members are bound by the company agreement whether or not they sign, but a Texas promise to contribute is enforceable only if signed by the person promising, so every principal who promises capital signs. An electronic signature satisfies a signature requirement where the signers agreed to deal electronically, and it is attributed to the person whose act it was; keep the signing service's record of who signed and when. File the signed agreement with the company's required records, which include its written company agreement and every amendment. This is the signature the company agreement step in form-sponsor-entity calls for.
steps.modeBasis: Signing is each principal's own act; an agent prepares the signature set and files the result.

steps.title: Sign and mail each 83(b) election within 30 days of the transfer
steps.instruction: The principal signs each 83(b) election and mails it to the IRS office where they file their own return no later than 30 days after the interest is transferred, giving the company its copy at the same time, and the holder too if the interest is issued to someone else. If the 30th day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, a postmark on the next day that is none of those is timely. Mail it by a service that proves the mailing date and keep that proof with the company's copy. An election cannot be revoked without the IRS's consent, and one mailed after the 30 days is not timely.
steps.modeBasis: The principal signs and mails the election; an agent cannot sign or mail it.
